entries.title: Genesis 48:3
segments: In sickness it is well gratefully to recount the past goodness of God to us and our families, and earnestly to recommend him and his salvation to all around us.

entries.title: Genesis 48:5
segments: They shall be mine; adopted as children and made heads of distinct tribes, like the other sons of Israel.

entries.title: Genesis 48:6
segments: After the name of their brethren; they should not be heads of distinct tribes, but should be reckoned as belonging to the tribe of Ephraim or of Manasseh.

entries.title: Genesis 48:8
segments: Beheld; he could discern that they were present, though he could not distinguish them.

entries.title: Genesis 48:11
segments: God is often better to us than our fears, and does more for us than we, in our ignorance and weakness, had dared to hope.  This should lead us to trust in him at all times, and in well-doing, patiently wait for his salvation.

entries.title: Genesis 48:12
segments: Bowed himself; in token of reverence for his father, from whom he was now to receive, in the persons of his sons, the paternal blessing.

entries.title: Genesis 48:15
segments: However much we may have of this world, and however many may minister to our wants, our daily bread comes from God, and he is the giver of all the common as well as special mercies of life.

entries.title: Genesis 48:16
segments: My name--and the name of my fathers; let them be called not Egyptians, but Israelites, descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and heirs of the promises made to them.

entries.title: Genesis 48:18
segments: Not so; he thought his father had made a mistake.

entries.title: Genesis 48:19
segments: Be greater; have a more numerous and powerful posterity.

entries.title: Genesis 48:21
segments: Strong confidence in the promises of God, and good hope through grace that when absent from the body we shall be present with the Lord, and that he will be the God of our children and children's children to coming generations, gives peace and joy in death.

entries.title: Genesis 48:22
segments: One portion; the Hebrew word rendered portion is shechem, which signifies shoulder, and also, as here, tract of land.  Thus Jacob points out this tract as the inheritance of Joseph.  Compare

.  Accordingly Joseph was buried here, Jos 24.32, and the whole adjacent country fell to the tribes of Ephrim and Manasseh. At the same time the words, "one portion above thy brethren," seem to intimate the double inheritance which Joseph should have in the land of Canaan through his two sons.

With my sword and with my bow; by warlike force.  There is an allusion here to the destruction of Shechem by Jacob's sons, which though disapproved by him, was yet, in the providence of God, designed to foreshadow the future conquest of Canaan by his children, to which these prophetic words look forward.
